q: As we go from left to right across the Periodic Table, the elements change in properties from metals to ____.
e: Periodic trends show a transition from metallic character on the left to non-metallic character on the right.

q: These elements except Al are called ____.
e: Metalloids lie along the stair-step line and exhibit properties of both metals and non-metals.

q: Hydrogen is also a ____.
e: Despite being in Group I, hydrogen is a gas and behaves as a non-metal.

q: Electronegativity is a measure of the tendency of an atom to attract a bonding pair of ____.
e: Electronegativity quantifies how strongly an atom pulls shared electrons in a chemical bond.

q: In the Periodic Table, in general, electronegativity of elements increases from left to right across a period, and from the bottom of a group to the ____.
e: Electronegativity is highest at the top right of the periodic table (excluding noble gases).

q: Atoms with high electronegativity tend to form ____ ions.
e: Highly electronegative atoms gain electrons to achieve a stable octet, becoming anions.

q: Atoms with low electronegativity, which is highly electropositive elements tend to form ____ ions.
e: Electropositive atoms lose electrons easily, forming cations.

q: The most electronegative element is ____.
e: Fluorine has the highest electronegativity value on the Pauling scale.

q: The least electronegative (most electropositive) element is ____.
e: Caesium (or francium) is at the bottom left, making it the most electropositive element.

q: The noble gases or inert gases are neither electropositive nor ____.
e: Noble gases have full valence shells and generally do not attract or lose electrons.

q: Atomic radii decrease from left to right across a ____.
e: Across a period, increasing nuclear charge pulls the electron cloud closer, shrinking the atom.

q: This is because ongoing from left to right across a period, the nuclear charge increases while the added electrons enter the ____ shell.
e: Electrons are added to the same principal energy level, so shielding does not increase significantly.

q: The increased nuclear charge attracts the electrons in the outermost shell closer to the nucleus, hence the shell ____ resulting in smaller atoms.
e: The stronger pull from the nucleus causes the electron cloud to contract.

q: The atomic radii increase from top to bottom down a group in the Periodic ____.
e: Moving down a group adds new principal energy levels, increasing atomic size.

q: This is because as the number of electrons increases, these additional electrons are in the larger electron shells making them farther and farther from the ____.
e: The addition of electron shells increases the distance between the nucleus and the valence electrons.

q: When one or more electrons are removed from a metal atom, a positive ion or ____ is formed.
e: Losing negative electrons leaves the atom with a net positive charge, forming a cation.

q: Thus, a positive ion is always ____ than its parent atoms.
e: With fewer electrons, electron-electron repulsion decreases, allowing the nucleus to pull the remaining electrons closer.

q: When one or more electrons are added to a neutral atom, a negative ion or ____ is formed.
e: Gaining negative electrons gives the atom a net negative charge, forming an anion.

q: Thus, a negative ion is always ____ than its parent atom.
e: Added electrons increase electron-electron repulsion, causing the electron cloud to expand.

q: The amount of energy required to remove an electron from a gaseous atom to form a gaseous ion is called the ____ energy.
e: Ionisation energy measures the strength of the hold the nucleus has on its outermost electron.

q: In general, ionisation energies increase from left to right across a ____.
e: Increasing nuclear charge across a period makes it harder to remove an electron.

q: In general, ionisation energies decrease down a ____.
e: Increased atomic size and shielding effect down a group make outer electrons easier to remove.

q: The noble gases have the highest ____ energies.
e: Noble gases have stable, full octets, requiring immense energy to disrupt.

q: The electron affinity of an element is the energy released when an electron is added to a gaseous atom to form a gaseous ____.
e: Electron affinity measures the energy change when an atom gains an electron.

q: The electron affinities generally increase from left to right across a ____.
e: Atoms on the right side of the table have a stronger attraction for additional electrons.

q: The electron affinity decreases on moving down a ____.
e: Larger atomic size down a group means the added electron is farther from the nucleus, reducing attraction.
